hypothesis: PENDING decompose: settings.json is lock-cycled 32-43x per fresh first turn (auth-lock record 20260927-075500, reported-only; merged b178174c5's #2915-pattern mutex serializes same-process holders but the cycles remain) from per-call SettingsManager rebuilds: every SettingsManager::create runs 2 scoped with_lock file-protocol cycles (global + project; the harness trial's project doc is absent, so 1 full cycle per create) even when the documents have not changed. TS keeps ONE SettingsManager per session-services instance (agent-session-services.ts:165, the AuthStorage sibling at :163) and serves every per-call getter from its in-memory snapshot (settings-manager.ts:582-588; provider-retry.ts:18-23) - zero per-turn lock cycles. A storage-layer read-through content cache (a pure-read trait arm, stat-validated per path - the auth-lock lane's proven pattern) should collapse the per-call read cycles to one miss per process per document with byte-identical file-protocol behavior for every writer and the port's per-call freshness preserved.
approach: Baseline decomposition first (no code changes): 31 trials on one VM at 58eda04c4 (12 fresh 1-turn + 8 fresh 2-turn timing legs, 4 timing-off controls, 3 strace legs, 2 diagnostic-build census legs with an env-gated pid/tid backtrace at FileSettingsStorage::with_lock; bench compare.msg_send mock-regime protocol replicated verbatim from the auth-lock lane incl. 120x40 PTY, probe-input-ready, typed prompt, Enter->first-chunk ack, needle+600ms-stability settle, PI_REQUEST_TIMING on; I/O advisory v1.0 preflights at every leg boundary). Candidate = 1 commit: C1 the settings read-through cache (settings/storage.rs + manager.rs load_scope). ABBA: 2-arm pair base vs C1 (A-B-B-A x3 rounds fresh 1-turn = 12/arm, 1 two-turn round = 4/arm, per-arm strace census pairs over ALL .lock surfaces - the unmasking census), same-VM sequential, sha-asserted binaries per leg, order-balanced rounds, unique per-leg output paths, zombie sweeps. Confirmation pair at the PR head after the fold.
parity_notes: Frozen parity untouched: the settings file protocol (proper-lockfile mkdir/utimensat/stale-reclaim/rmdir, the 10x20ms retry structure, atomic_write temp+rename+private-mode) is byte-for-byte unchanged for every writer; with_lock (every write and read-modify-write flow) is untouched; session JSONL, RLM wire, prompts, TUI behavior unchanged (the delta touches only crates/pa-core/src/settings/storage.rs + the load_scope call in manager.rs). The pure-read arm (SettingsStorage::read, default = the old with_lock read) is used ONLY by load_scope (from_storage + reload). TS-parity case FIRST: TS constructs ONE SettingsManager per session-services instance and serves every per-call getter from its in-memory snapshot (agent-session-services.ts:165; getGlobalSettings/getProjectSettings settings-manager.ts:582-588; provider-retry.ts:18-23; the file protocol runs only at construction + explicit reloads, settings-manager.ts:493-500); the port's ~100 SettingsManager::create call sites rebuild the whole manager per call (each = 2 scoped with_lock loads) - a port artifact with no TS counterpart benefit. The stat-validated cache keeps the port's per-call freshness STRICTLY fresher than the TS snapshot instance (an external write invalidates on the next read via dev/ino/mtime_ns/len identity; TS never re-reads). Documented behavior delta: a cache hit now succeeds under a foreign lock holder while the document is unchanged (TS serves its snapshot in exactly that window); first reads in a process (cache misses) keep the old contention behavior. Same-ns edge (theoretical: an in-place rewrite within mtime-ns granularity with identical length) - the auth-lock reviewers' accepted-with-note class, far tighter than the TS unvalidated snapshot. No callback re-entrancy: the read arm has NO callback; the process mutex is a leaf and shared with with_lock (same registry), so read+write order in-process; per-instance manager mutable state untouched (each create still parses + merges + tracks its own runtime overrides; only the file protocol cycles collapse). 3 new unit tests: write-through invalidation, external in-place + atomic-rename invalidation, absent-file Ok(None) + with_lock error-class parity, and the trait-default read on the in-memory backend.
